summary: Debugged the registry's spawn-git-ENOENT error caused by using a nonexistent clone directory as cwd in registry-manager.ts, confirmed gizmo.registry.json was untracked and missing from the clone, committed both fixes, and verified the full registry add/update/link/unlink loop end-to-end via WebSocket probes against the restarted dev server. Final state: ask-user extension installed (ask-user.ts + ask-user.web.js) in ~/.pi/agent/extensions/, pnpm check clean, 70 vitest tests passing, two commits landed.
decisions: registry-manager.ts clone uses cloneHome() as exec cwd (not the target clone path) so the directory exists at spawn time — fixes the spawn git ENOENT

Committed gizmo.registry.json alongside the cwd fix so the registry manifest is present in the clone and readRegistryManifest picks up extensionsDir: 'pi-extensions' instead of defaulting to 'extensions'
Restarted the dev server (stop+start) before probing because tsx-watch had failed to reload the diagnostic code
Full registry loop verified via WebSocket probes: add, update (pull), link, unlink, relink — all ok
errors: spawn git ENOENT on registry.add — caused by registry-manager.ts passing the target clone directory as exec cwd before it existed; fixed by using cloneHome()

registry.link ENOENT on pi-extension.ts — caused by gizmo.registry.json being untracked so the clone had no manifest and defaulted to extensionsDir 'extensions' instead of 'pi-extensions'; fixed by committing the manifest
Probe TypeError on .slice of undefined — fixed by JSON.stringify-ing the whole added response instead of dereferencing .result
git commit failed with .git/index.lock present — resolved by removing the stale lock file
